name: Aoligei (奥利给)
blurb: A Chinese cheer meaning "let's go!", from a short-video creator's sign-off in 2019
title: Aoligei (奥利给) Meme: Meaning, Origin & Trend
description: Aoligei (奥利给) is a Chinese cheer like "let's go!". It comes from a Kuaishou winter swimmer's 2019 sign-off and peaked around the 2020 New Year.
h1: What is the Aoligei (奥利给) meme?
answer: Aoligei (奥利给, also written 奥力给) is a Chinese internet cheer that means roughly "let's go!" or "you've got this!". It comes from 朝阳冬泳怪鸽 (Zhaoyang Dongyong Guaige, "the winter-swimming pigeon of Chaoyang"), a middle-aged winter swimmer from Liaoning who began posting on Kuaishou in January 2019 and ended his pep talks with "no problem, just do it! Go! Aoligei!". Remixes of his clips on Bilibili spread the word in 2019, and it peaked around the 2020 New Year, when a CCTV news anchor said "Chinese spaceflight, aoligei!".

body: The source clips show a man in swimming trunks by a frozen river in Liaoning, delivering loud motivational lines straight to the camera: do not fear difficulties, face them with a smile, the best way to beat fear is to face it. Each talk ends with a shout of "加油！奥力给！" (Go! Aoligei!).

The word has no dictionary meaning. A common explanation online is that it is 给力嗷 (geili ao, "awesome!") said backwards, but in practice it is simply an energetic cheer, used both sincerely and with a wink.

head: Date
Event
rows: Zhaoyang Dongyong Guaige starts posting winter-swimming and pep-talk videos on Kuaishou and other short-video apps
A Bilibili compilation of his pep talks, "正能量语录奥利给", is uploaded on 20 May; it later passes 30 million views
Bilibili creators turn his clips into remixes (guichu), spreading the word far beyond Kuaishou
CCTV anchor Kang Hui ends a 主播说联播 segment on a rocket launch with "Chinese spaceflight, aoligei!"
The Paper visits him in Chaoyang and films him shouting the slogan
Kuaishou releases a brand film with him as narrator, titled 看见 (Seen) or 自己的英雄

ul: Before an exam or a hard task: "明天考试，奥利给！" (Exam tomorrow, let's go!)
Cheering a team, an athlete or a national achievement in comments
Self-mocking motivation: "Monday again. Aoligei, I guess."
Quoting the full catchphrase: "没毛病，干就完了！加油！奥利给！"

body: Aoligei peaked in 2019–2020 and is now a familiar classic of Chinese meme culture rather than a fresh joke. People still drop it as a playful "let's go", often with a nostalgic or ironic tone. The creator kept posting from his hometown after becoming famous.

faq.q: What does aoligei mean in English?
faq.a: Roughly "let's go!" or "you've got this!". It is a cheer, not a word with a fixed dictionary meaning.
The Kuaishou creator 朝阳冬泳怪鸽 (Zhaoyang Dongyong Guaige), a winter swimmer from Liaoning who ended his 2019 pep-talk videos with it.

faq.q: Is it 奥利给 or 奥力给?
faq.a: Both spellings are used. The creator's own catchphrase is often written 奥力给; 奥利给 is the more common spelling online.
